value: ヴィンランド・サガ (Vinrando Saga)
text: Vinland Saga is written ヴィンランド・サガ in Japanese and read Vinrando Saga.
excerpt: Vinland Saga (ヴィンランド・サガ, Vinrando Saga) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Makoto Yukimura.

text: Makoto Yukimura writes and draws the manga, which Kodansha publishes; his name is 幸村誠 in Japanese.
excerpt: written and illustrated by Makoto Yukimura. The series is published by Kodansha

value: Weekly Shōnen Magazine from April 13, 2005; Monthly Afternoon from December 24, 2005 to July 25, 2025
text: The manga began in Weekly Shōnen Magazine in April 2005, moved to Monthly Afternoon on December 24, 2005, and finished there on July 25, 2025.
excerpt: starting on December 24, 2005. The series finished after 20 years of publication on July 25, 2025.

value: 29 volumes and 220 chapters; final volume on September 22, 2025
text: The story is collected in 29 volumes holding 220 chapters, and the last volume came out on September 22, 2025.
excerpt: As of September 2025, the chapters have been collected in twenty-nine tankobon volumes.

value: Wit Studio, director Shūhei Yabuta, 24 episodes, July 8 to December 30, 2019
text: Wit Studio animated the first season under director Shūhei Yabuta; its 24 episodes were shown on NHK General TV from July 8 to December 30, 2019.
excerpt: The series ran for 24 episodes on NHK General TV, premiering July 8, 2019, with the first three episodes, and concluding on December 30 of that same year.

value: MAPPA, 24 episodes (overall 25 to 48, 48 in total), January 10 to June 20, 2023
text: MAPPA took over for the second season, which aired 24 more episodes, numbered 25 to 48 overall, from January 10 to June 20, 2023.
excerpt: On May 5, 2022, it was announced that MAPPA would be taking over for the second season of the series. It aired from January 10 to June 20, 2023

value: OP 1: Mukanjyo - Survive Said the Prophet (season 1)
OP 2: Dark Crow - Man with a Mission (season 1)
text: Season one opened with Mukanjyo by Survive Said the Prophet and later Dark Crow by Man with a Mission, and closed with Torches by Aimer and later Drown by milet.
excerpt: The first opening theme of the TV series "Mukanjyo" by Survive Said the Prophet, while the first ending theme is "Torches" by Aimer.

value: OP 4: Paradox - Survive Said the Prophet (season 2)
text: Season two used River by Anonymouz and then Paradox by Survive Said the Prophet as openings, with Without Love by LMYK and Ember by haju:harmonics as endings.
excerpt: For the second season, the first opening theme is "River" by Anonymouz, while the first ending theme is "Without Love" by LMYK.

text: The manga article divides the plot into four arcs: the War Arc, the Slave Arc, the Eastern Expedition Arc and the Vinland Arc.
excerpt: While Thorfinn's appearance evolved across the series' four arcs, Yukimura focused intently on his psychological development.

value: War Arc: chapters 1 to 54, anime episodes 1 to 24
Slave Arc: chapters 55 to 100, anime episodes 25 to 48
Eastern Expedition Arc: chapters 101 to 160, manga only
Vinland Arc: chapters 161 to 220, manga only
text: Using the numbered chapter list, the War Arc fills chapters 1 to 54 (season one) and the Slave Arc chapters 55 to 100 (season two); the last two arcs are not animated yet.
excerpt: 054. End of the Prologue. 055. Slave. 099. Departure. 100. Homecoming. 101. The Fettered Tern (1). 161. Sigurd's Decision

text: The character list gives each name with its katakana spelling; these twelve appear here, sorted by the story arc in which they are introduced.
excerpt: Thorfinn (トルフィン, Torufin), Askeladd (アシェラッド, Asheraddo), Bjorn (ビョルン, Byorun), Canute (クヌート, Kunūto)

value: Over 7 million copies by August 2022; Japan Media Arts Festival Grand Prize, 2009; Kodansha Manga Award, 2012
text: In 2009 the Japan Media Arts Festival gave the manga its top honor, and Kodansha's general-manga prize followed in 2012; circulation topped 7 million copies by August 2022.
excerpt: The series won the 13th Japan Media Arts Festival's Grand Prize in 2009 and the 36th Kodansha Manga Award for Best General Manga in 2012.

value: Kodansha USA, two-in-one hardcovers from October 14, 2013
text: Kodansha USA publishes the manga in English in two-in-one hardcovers, starting on October 14, 2013.
excerpt: The first volume was published on October 14, 2013.

value: Inspired by a real Icelandic explorer, Thorfinn Karlsefni
text: The series dramatizes the expedition of the real Icelandic explorer Thorfinn Karlsefni, and the lead is a fictional counterpart of him.
excerpt: The series is a dramatization of the story of the Icelandic explorer Thorfinn Karlsefni and his expedition to find Vinland.

text: Thors earned the epithet the Troll of Jom as a Jomsviking general, then quietly left war behind to live as a pacifist farmer.
excerpt: Thors is a Jomsviking general whose phenomenal combat prowess earns him the epithet "The Troll of Jom".
